hypothesis: In the 5 minutes after a Binance USDS-M liquidation of at least 250 000 USD, the price reverses against the direction of the forced flow (up after a liquidated long, down after a liquidated short) by more than 10 bps gross, measured from the first trade at least 2 seconds after the exchange event timestamp, because an extreme forced order overshoots the fair price and liquidity providers fade it once the forced flow is absorbed.
economic_reason: An extreme liquidation is a price-insensitive order far larger than the resting book; it prints an overshoot. Once the forced flow stops, market makers and arbitrageurs restore the price toward other venues and the index. The payer is the liquidated account (and the momentum traders who chased the print). If the overshoot is already gone 2 seconds after the message, the verdict is REJECTED_NO_GROSS.

entry_rule.price: first aggTrade at or after entry time (10 s, then 60 s lookahead, else excluded)
entry_rule.direction: against the forced flow: buy after a liquidated long, sell after a liquidated short

exit_rule.price: last aggTrade at or before exit time

cost_model.notes: VIP0 USDS-M taker 5 bps per side; spread taken PER EVENT from the tape (spread_before_bps, median 0.1 bps on the universe); slippage 4 bps declared; round trip = 10 + spread_i + 4

validation_window.nature: one session of the live forced-flow tape, frozen (sha b78d1b50…); one sealed look

declustering_rule.note: a cascade hits many symbols at once: the 5-minute window across symbols is the unit of independence

notes: RESEARCH_ONLY. First-look hypothesis H2 of the same PREREG. Universe: 62 events in 15 clusters: below the 20-cluster floor, so FORWARD_SEAL_REQUIRED is impossible on this tape by construction; only a rejection is a result here.
